newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-NAB sees huge upside in UK-Irish ops.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-NAB sees huge upside in UK-Irish ops.

text.p: National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB) managing director Don Argus said on Thursday the expected efficiency gains over the next 18 months from its United Kingdom and Ireland operations.
NAB owns the Yorkshire Bank, the Clydesdale Bank in England, the National Irish Bank in Ireland and the Northern Bank in Northern Ireland.

"I think you will now start to see hopefully in the next 12 to 18 months the real effect of the economies of scale that you can drive out of those four banks in that environment," Argus told reporters after the bank released its annual results.
"It's got a huge upside over there," Argus said.
NAB said operating profit of its United Kingdom and Ireland banking and financial services group fell four percent to A$403 million in the year to September 30, 1996.
Argus said the results from the UK and Ireland were largely affected by the higher Australian dollar, as in local currency terms the operations reported higher earnings.
"Whilst the currency translation has had an effect on the headline numbers, I can assure you they have done particularly well in their market place," Argus said.
Argus said NAB had upgraded its wholesale banking activities in the UK and Ireland and expected to make an announcement soon about its global wholesale bank.
He said NAB also planned to start a telephone banking service in the UK and Ireland.
NAB reported a 6.8 percent rise in net profit to A$2.1 billion in 1995/96.
At 3.20 p.m. (0420 GMT), NAB shares were 22 cents or 1.58 percent higher at A$14.14 with 3.77 million shares traded.
